subject: Tier slotting & feature-credit clarification for Lighthouse pilot
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@lighthousehealth.com>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-09-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Compact -> Elastic upgrade questions and credits

Hi Lauren —

Thanks again for the quick demo yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our side as we evaluate moving Lighthouse Health from Compact to an Elastic/Hybrid setup:

- We want to avoid unpredictable token spikes. Can you outline how "tier slotting" would work for us (mixing committed throughput with on-demand)?
- How do feature bundles (priority burst, extended observability retention) get credited or priced when we change tiers?
- What is Redwood's approach to proration during an upgrade or downgrade? Any standard migration credits?

I attached our Q3 usage export so you can model the scenarios. Ideally we get a short illustration (2 scenarios) and a proposed next step (pilot length, credit, and rollback guardrails).

Can we aim for a call next week to walk through an illustration?

Thanks,
Sarah
Director, Platform Integrations
Lighthouse Health
[attachment: usage_report_Q3.csv]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@lighthousehealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-09-29T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Compact -> Elastic upgrade questions and credits

Hi Sarah — thanks for the export, that helps. High-level options we usually propose: 

Option A — Step upgrade (low friction)
- Move to Elastic tier with committed baseline equal to 60% of current 95th percentile usage.
- On-demand tokens for peaks; billing at on-demand rates above committed baseline.
- One-time migration credit equal to ~10% of estimated 3 months committed spend to offset cutover costs.

Option B — Hybrid slotting (cost predictability + burst)
- Keep Compact baseline, add a dedicated "slot" pool for critical endpoints (reserved throughput for peak traffic).
- Feature bundle (priority burst + 90-day extended retention) as an add-on with a bundled discount if committed for 6+ months.

Quick ask: which of the two risk profiles matches your org — "avoid any burst spend surprises" (Option B) or "simpler immediate lift with some on-demand exposure" (Option A)? Once you tell me that, Ben will sketch numbers and Marissa can propose contractual guardrails for rollback/proration.

Happy to book 30 minutes — I have availability Tue/Wed next week.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@lighthousehealth.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2025-09-29T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Compact -> Elastic upgrade questions and credits (pricing sketch attached)

Sarah — looping in pricing details. Attached is a quick sketch. Top-line: 

- Scenario 1 (Step upgrade): estimated committed baseline $26k/mo, on-demand estimate $6k/mo (95th->peaks). Suggested migration credit: one-time $7.8k (≈10% * 3 mo committed).
- Scenario 2 (Hybrid slotting + feature bundle): reserved slot pool $12k/mo + feature bundle $2k/mo; if you commit 12 months we can apply a 15% committed discount to the dedicated portion (net effective annual savings).

Contract levers we can offer:
- 90-day pilot with a pro-rated invoice (no penalty for rollback within pilot).
- If you sign a 12-month reserved commitment, we can include a one-time onboarding credit and increased observability retention as part of the bundle.

I attached the line-item sketch so you can see the math. If you'd like, we can convert Scenario 2 to a 6-month pilot with a smaller discount (7%) and the same rollback guardrail.

- Ben
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[attachment: pricing_sketch.xlsx]

From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@lighthousehealth.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2025-09-30T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Compact -> Elastic upgrade questions and credits (pricing sketch attached)

Thanks Ben — the sketches are helpful. A couple follow-ups before we loop procurement: 

1) Feature bundle detail: priority burst = guaranteed slot for up to 30% additional throughput for X seconds / minute — will that be charged at on-demand rates on top of bundle? How is that metered?
2) Observability: If we take the 90-day pilot with extended retention as part of the bundle, can that retention persist if we roll back? We need logs for audits and would like exportability.
3) Rollback language: procurement will ask for a clear clause that allows us to step back to Compact within the pilot window with pro-rated billing and a defined data retention/export policy.

If you can confirm answers to 1–3 and share a one-pager (legal-friendly) we can get procurement onboard. We are leaning to Scenario 2 but want the pilot guardrails spelled out.

— Sarah

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@lighthousehealth.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2025-10-01T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Compact -> Elastic upgrade questions and credits — pilot guardrails

Hi Sarah — quick clarifications to address procurement items: 

1) Priority burst metering: the bundle includes an assigned burst bucket applied at the request-routing layer. If burst usage exceeds the assigned bucket in a billing cycle, overage is billed at on-demand token rates. We'll show an example in the MAP.

2) Observability retention: for pilot customers we can enable extended retention for 90 days. If you decide to roll back during the pilot, we will retain data for an additional 30 days and provide an export (JSON/CSV) to your S3 endpoint. We will include export instructions in the MAP.

3) Rollback clause (contract language):
- 90-day pilot window where Lighthouse may elect to revert to Compact with pro-rated billing for committed capacity.
- No termination fee inside pilot; migration credit remains as a one-time credit applied if you complete >60 days.
- Post-pilot rollback: standard notice and 30-day proration applies.

Pilot mechanics we recommend: 90 days, 30% burst capacity for first 30 days, mutual action plan with milestones (onboarding, traffic mig, QA, sign-off). I've attached the MAP for your review and included a draft legal-friendly rollback paragraph.

Next steps: if that looks good I can push the MAP to the shared Drive and we can generate a DocuSign envelope with the pilot addendum.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
